definition: VP-Expert is an artificial intelligence development tool that gained popularity in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
details: Published by Paperback Software, VP-Expert was designed to facilitate the creation of rule-based expert systems, primarily for applications in business and industry. It was the best-selling expert-system software for microcomputers in the late 1980s.

explainer.lead: VP-Expert was an AI development tool published by Paperback Software that made rule-based expert systems accessible on microcomputers. It was the best-selling expert-system software for microcomputers in the late 1980s.

tiers.eli5: It was a program people used to write down rules for a computer so it could give expert-style advice, mainly for business tasks.
tiers.practitioner: Developers used it to build rule-based expert systems for business and industry applications. Its age means modern engineers treat it as historical rather than a current platform.
tiers.paperLevel: A rule-based expert-system development tool published by Paperback Software, popular in the late 1980s and early 1990s; best-selling expert-system software for microcomputers in the late 1980s.

explainer.example: A business could encode its decision rules in VP-Expert and have the resulting system answer queries by applying those rules.
